entities.summary: Frederick Biletnikoff is an American former professional football player and coach. He played as a wide receiver for the Oakland Raiders in the American Football League (AFL) and National Football League (NFL) for 14 seasons and later was an assistant coach with the team. He retired as an NFL player after the 1978 season then played one more season in the Canadian Football League (CFL) for the Montreal Alouettes in 1980. While he lacked the breakaway speed to be a deep-play threat, Biletnikoff was one of the most sure-handed and consistent receivers of his day with a propensity for making spectacular catches.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the Oakland Raiders' dynasty of the 1970s, Biletnikoff's consistent and sure-handed play helped shape the team's identity during a pivotal era for American football. His legacy continues to influence the sport today.
